audit.why: EVEN / 6/10 with a 7/10 carry threat is the right shape at 54.14% over 181 games: Quinn's win rate comes from level 1-2 tempo and R roams, not from winning the lane, which the prose states outright ('Maokai just refuses to lose the lane').
audit.corrected: Ratings unchanged; the mirror set its own side to EVEN 5/10, which is consistent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 5 and 6 read Quinn and rows 3, 4 read Skill, while their own captions say 'you no longer win the straight trade', 'his sustain out-values your poke', 'at 6 you can't duel his R-fed sustain', and 'your lethality spike can't burst a healing Maokai'.
audit.why: Packet chart is Skill, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Skill and the audited mirror moved rows 1-5 to Maokai with row 6 left at Skill. The recorded 'chart contradicts data' defect is resolved by the two-item row being a genuine coin flip, which whys[6] already says.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 to Maokai and row 6 to Skill, in matched full/content pairs; row 0 stays Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Dodge it' is wrong advice — Twisted Advance is targeted and Maokai is untargetable during it, so it cannot be sidestepped once cast. Also missing: Bramble Smash grounds, which denies Vault, and both his W and R cancel Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Kit: W 'contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target', 14s at rank 1, flagged hardCC and untargetable. Q flagged grounding, 7s down to 5s. R flagged hardCC. Quinn's R is a channel any CC cancels, and Vault is a dash.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and dontsFull[0..1].d now say it must be baited rather than dodged, name the grounding on Bramble Smash, give Sapling Toss's 1100 range and 18s, and state exactly what the blind does not stop.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on the ability the whole page is built around.
audit.why: Twisted Advance 14s at rank 1, Bramble Smash 7s down to 5s, Sapling Toss 18s at rank 1, Nature's Grasp 130s.
audit.corrected: Written into the cooldown block, the do's, the don'ts and report[5].

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1 — targeted and untargetable, so it cannot be sidestepped once cast. - Bramble Smash: 7s to 5s, and it grounds Vault. - His W and R both cancel your ult.

edits.before: His lock-on root. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Targeted and untargetable — 14s at rank 1, so bait it, don't dodge.

edits.before: Track Maokai's Twisted Advance (Root): His lock-on root. Dodge it. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is targeted, so it cannot be sidestepped — bait the 14s. Bramble Smash grounds Vault.

edits.before: That is Maokai's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: The blind stops only his autos and the Sap Magic proc — W, Q and R all land.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Sapling Toss reaches 1100 and knocks you up — 18s at rank 1.

notes: The mirror's key insight is carried over rather than re-derived: 'dodge his blind' style advice teaches players to hold their whole combo when Blinding Assault only affects basic attacks — Bramble Smash, Twisted Advance and Nature's Grasp all land through it, and the Sap Magic proc is the one thing the blind actually costs him. Anti-heal advice in report[8] is correct and untouched: Sap Magic is a real heal on a cooldown that shortens every time he casts or is hit by a spell.
